minutes.headline: Commission authorized the chair and Bob to ask the select board for more admin hours; Holman Street got an enforcement order.
minutes.summary: The meeting began with a SharePoint training for members, then covered continuances, two requests for determination (a fence and a dock), a tree-removal request continued for a site walk, and the 390 Howard Street consultant escrow. The commission voted an enforcement order and denied a certificate of compliance for the Holman Street lots over failed erosion control. It also authorized two members to pitch more office hours and consultant reviews to the select board, discussed moving to OpenGov, and declined to recommend acquiring a Chapter 61 parcel.

public_comment.topic: Chair invited public comment; none was offered.

budget_items.what_was_said: Applicant agreed to pay the third-party consultant's quote via a 53G account, and agreed to cover overruns.
The town already pays a flat subscription, so adding conservation workflows would add no cost.
Commission discussed raising the clerical hours and noted departments were told to level-fund because of the school budget.
A member suggested asking to roll over unspent conservation payroll to fund temporary help.
A member said the bylaw sets a maximum peer review fee based on project cost.

decisions.decision: No vote needed on EcoTech clarification; the administrator is to set up the 53G escrow account for 390 Howard Street.
Sophie to return March 20 with a proposal and timeline for moving applications to OpenGov; vote deferred until then.
Guidance to Sophie on 141 Hemlock: seek a written continuance request with failure-to-appear language, and research the still-active order of conditions.
Sophie to contact the neighbor of 141 Hemlock informally about trees cut across the property line.
Third batch of encroachment issues left for members to discuss offline; Sophie to notify the attorney about the returned 315 Lancaster letter.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to have the chair and Bob ask the select board for more administrative hours and consultant review, and the vote was unanimous.
It authorized an enforcement order over a failed silt fence and silt runoff at the Holman Street lots, then denied a certificate of compliance for lots three and four without prejudice.
The commission voted to tell open space, the planning board and the select board it has no intent to acquire the 100 Howard Street Chapter 61 parcel.
The 390 Howard Street applicant agreed to pay a third-party consultant through a 53G escrow account and to cover overruns; the administrator is to set up the account.
A dock at 735 Flat Hill Road got a negative determination on a 4-1 vote, and a decision on moving applications to OpenGov was deferred to March 20.

why_it_matters: Staffing for the Conservation Commission's reviews depends on a request to the select board at a time when departments were told to level-fund because of the school budget, so a resident with a wetlands filing may see the pace of reviews tied to that decision.

The Holman Street enforcement order and the denied certificate show the commission acting on erosion control at a development site, and the 53G escrow shows the applicant, not the town, paying for outside review at 390 Howard Street.
watch_next: March 20: the commission takes up Sophie's proposal and timeline for moving applications to OpenGov, with the vote deferred to that meeting.
The select board's response to the request for added administrative hours and consultant review.
